humanities_role_explanation: Questions span general topics (science & technology, politics, art, geography, sports, music, TV, history, video games); humanities topics (Art n=550, History n=173) only supply items for generic short-form factuality testing, not disciplinary competence.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only short fact-seeking questions with short text reference answers.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Short-form fact-seeking QA with a single indisputable answer (open-ended short answer, graded correct/incorrect/not attempted); also measures calibration via stated confidence and answer frequency ('know what they know').

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Broad multi-topic factuality benchmark spanning many domains, though scoped to one task format (short-form factual QA).

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Claude-3 haiku/sonnet/opus, Claude-3.5-sonnet, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, o1-mini, o1-preview.

quantitative_metrics.note: Correct, not attempted, incorrect, correct given attempted, F-score, calibration plots.

summary: SimpleQA is a benchmark of 4,326 short, fact-seeking questions with single, indisputable answers, adversarially collected against GPT-4 responses. It evaluates OpenAI and Anthropic models with a prompted ChatGPT grader and also measures calibration.
key_findings: Frontier models score low: o1-preview 42.7% correct (F-score 44.8), GPT-4o 38.2%, Claude-3.5-sonnet 28.9%. Claude models abstain more often. Models overstate confidence, and o1-preview is the best calibrated.
facets_explanation: AI trainers (human annotators hired by OpenAI) wrote the questions and answers with supporting web links; a second independent trainer answered, and only matching items were kept. Items with ambiguity, multiple answers or contradictory sources were removed or counted as errors (estimated error rate ~3%). The questions require external world knowledge not given in the prompt. Authors are not the annotators, but the closest value among the allowed options is paper_authors; the annotators were AI trainers working for OpenAI.
results_explanation: Table 3 reports OpenAI o1-preview with Correct 42.7, Not attempted 9.2, Incorrect 48.1, Correct given attempted 47.0 and F-score 44.8; the headline is overall correct, treated here as accuracy. No format comparison on the same items is reported, and the third-trainer check (94.4%) is a data-quality check, not a human baseline for models.

humanities_role.quote: The most common topics were Science & Technology (n=858), Politics (n=709), and Art (n=550).

dataset_size.quote: We present a benchmark called SimpleQA, which contains 4,326 short, fact-seeking questions.

evaluation_set_size.quote: We present a benchmark called SimpleQA, which contains 4,326 short, fact-seeking questions.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: Please give your best guess, along with your confidence as a percentage that that is the correct answer

gold_source.quote: First, AI trainers (i.e., human annotators) created question and answer pairs.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: Here we only focus on objective knowledge and force questions to be written such that they only have a single, indisputable answer.

answer_multiplicity.quote: questions are created such that there exists only a single, indisputable answer

plurality_treatment.quote: Only questions where the answers from both AI trainers were the same were kept in the dataset.
